title: Refurbishment Finance UK
summary: Service page for Silver Oak Capital's refurbishment finance, presented as a short-term bridging loan covering the purchase price of a property and typically 100% of build costs, with works funds released in stages/in arrears after inspection and interest rolled up or retained until sale or refinance. The page segments works into light (cosmetic, no building regs or planning), medium (beyond cosmetic, usually under Permitted Development Rights, often needing building regs approval) and heavy (extending the footprint or changing the roofline, e.g. dormer loft conversion). Search excerpts reveal no rates, fees, minimum loan size or LTV for this page; the heavy tier text was truncated in results. Search (c) surfaced nothing about the firm.

sections.heading: Overview / bespoke refurbishment finance (light, medium, heavy)
sections.content: [a][b] 'Silver Oak Capital specialises in securing bespoke refurbishment finance solutions across the entire spectrum – light, medium, and heavy.' [a][b] The firm says it can fund up to 100% of build costs, released in stages. [a] The product is described as a short-term bridging loan that 'covers the purchase price of a property and typically 100% of the build costs'.

sections.heading: Light refurbishment
sections.content: [a] 'purely cosmetic updates that do not require building regulations or planning permission' - examples given: kitchens, bathrooms, decorating, flooring. [b] Examples repeated: kitchens, bathrooms, redecorating; the page notes these loans are typically quick to arrange with light monitoring (tool paraphrase).

sections.heading: Medium refurbishment
sections.content: [a][b] Works that go beyond cosmetic changes but stop short of major structural work; they 'often require building regulations approval but usually rely on Permitted Development Rights (PDRs)' rather than full planning permission.

sections.heading: Heavy refurbishment
sections.content: [a] Attributed by the search tool to 'the firm's FAQ': 'extending the footprint (extension) or changing the roofline (dormer loft conversion), it is Heavy.' [b] The heavy tier's details were cut off in results; nothing further revealed.

sections.heading: Interest and repayment
sections.content: [a] 'the interest is typically rolled up or retained' - interest is generally not paid monthly and is settled when the property is sold or refinanced at the end of the project. [b] (FAQ page per tool) no monthly payments are due during works.

sections.heading: Drawdowns / release of build costs
sections.content: [a] 'most lenders will advance 100% of the build costs. These are released in arrears' - build costs are reimbursed in arrears after an inspection, provided the end value supports the loan. [b] The lender reimburses after an inspection; funds released in stages.

sections.heading: Loan term
sections.content: [b] Described as a bridging loan that is a short-term facility (up to 12-24 months). [b] Another site page puts general bridging terms at between 1 and 36 months.

sections.heading: Related: HMO refurbishment bridging (from /hmo-finance/)
sections.content: [b] The HMO finance page says Silver Oak arranges refurbishment bridging finance for the purchase and works, and pre-agrees the exit onto a long-term HMO mortgage (tool paraphrase).
